question: I bought two frocks for ₹1,200. I sold the first one at a loss of 10% and the second at a gain of 15%. If, on the whole I made neither a loss nor a gain, find the cost price (in ₹) of the first frock.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When there is neither profit nor loss, absolute loss equals absolute profit.

CP₁ × 10% = CP₂ × 15% ⇒ CP₁ : CP₂ = 15 : 10 = 3 : 2

Total ratio parts = 3 + 2 = 5 parts

5 parts = ₹1200 ⇒ 1 part = ₹240

CP of the first frock (3 parts) = 3 × 240 = ₹720

**∴ The correct answer is ₹720.**

**Given:**

Total CP of two frocks = ₹1200

Loss on the first frock = 10%

Gain on the second frock = 15%

Overall transaction = No profit and no loss

**Formula Used:**

When overall outcome is 0% profit/loss, Loss Amount = Profit Amount.

**Calculations:**

Let the CP of the first frock be x.

Then, the CP of the second frock is (1200 − x).

⇒ Loss on 1st = Gain on 2nd

⇒ 10% of x = 15% of (1200 − x)

⇒ (10 ÷ 100) × x = (15 ÷ 100) × (1200 − x)

⇒ 10x = 15 × (1200 − x)

⇒ 10x = 18000 − 15x

⇒ 25x = 18000

⇒ x = 18000 ÷ 25 = 720

**∴ The correct answer is ₹720.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

No Profit No Loss Case

When a transaction results in neither a net gain nor a net loss, the absolute financial loss incurred on one item exactly counterbalances the absolute financial gain on the other. Therefore, CP₁ × Loss% = CP₂ × Profit%.

Alligation Method for Profit and Loss

Applying the rule of alligation on profit and loss percentages directly yields the ratio of the Cost Prices (CP) of the respective items. Loss values are taken as negative, while profit values are positive.

Successive Percentage Change

If the price of a single item is changed successively by P% profit and L% loss, the net effect can be evaluated using the equivalent percentage formula: (P − L − (P×L)÷100)%.
